relevance_note: One cohort patient carries a germline TNFAIP3 variant with individual-level detail: 'WES revealed a heterozygous c.559C>T (p. Q187X) mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene in patient 7, which is from her father'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Tables 1-3 (clinical, laboratory and immunologic features per patient) appear only as headings in this file, with no content, so per-patient details from them (age at onset, CRP/ESR, skin and joint findings) are unavailable and recorded as not reported. Scope: of the 7 enrolled SLE-with-lymphoproliferation patients, only patient 7 carries a TNFAIP3 variant (patients 1-4 somatic NRAS, patient 6 germline PIK3CD, patient 5 none); they get no rows (cohort_size_as_stated = 7). In-scope relatives: the father (the variant 'is from her father') and patient 7's grandparents (tested negative). The paper says only 'grandparents' (plural) and does not say how many or which side, so two rows are given (the minimum the plural implies) and labelled 'grandparent of patient 7' and 'grandparent of patient 7 2'. Group-derived phenotypes for patient 7: recurrent fever and hematologic involvement (cytopenia) are 6/6 among 'patients with mutations' (patients 1-4, 6, 7), which matches 6/7 overall with patient 5 stated to have neither; renal involvement 7/7, ANA >=1:320 'in all patients', elevated IgG 'in all patients', hepatomegaly and/or splenomegaly and/or lymphadenectasis 'All patients', increased IgE 'the other patients' besides patient 3, and no malignant cells on bone marrow aspiration 'in all patients'. The checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is marked observed from this SLE hematologic involvement, though the paper does not call patient 7's cytopenia autoimmune. Enrolment as 'SLE with lymphoproliferation' was not used as evidence (study criteria); lymphoproliferation rests on the result statement 'All patients had hepatomegaly and/or splenomegaly and/or lymphadenectasis.' Counts without names (skin involvement in 2/7 and 1/6; monocytosis in 'almost all patients') were not attributed to anyone. Sex of patient 7 comes from the pronouns 'her father' and 'her grandparents'. is_proband is null for patient 7 because the paper never uses 'proband' or 'index case'. Patient 7's diagnosis as stated in this paper is SLE with lymphoproliferation; the paper does not give her an HA20 diagnosis in so many words (it says TNFAIP3 mutations cause haploinsufficiency of A20 in general). The protein change is printed both as 'p.Q187X' (Results, Abstract) and 'p. Q187X' (Discussion); the Sanger section prints '559C>T' without 'c.'. No transcript is printed. The father's zygosity and the origin of his variant are not stated, and the paper does not say whether the grandparents are his parents. Prior reports: patient 7 'was reported in our previous study' (ref 18); patient 6 (PIK3CD, out of scope) was also previously reported (ref 23), not recorded in prior_report_citation. Contradiction in the paper (NRAS, out of scope): the NRAS variant is given as 'c.38 A>G, p.G13C' in the text but 'c.38G>A, p.G13D' in the Figure 2 and 3 legends. No contradiction found for patient 7 or the TNFAIP3 variant.
